finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL. The only check is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io"), which matches anywhere in the string. An attacker can reach any host, including internal services and cloud metadata, and the response body is returned to them (full-read SSRF). Redirects are also followed because the default client is used.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response copied to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: Only check is a substring match for "example.io". It does not parse the URL or check scheme or host. Payloads such as http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://127.0.0.1:8080/#example.io or http://evil.com/example.io pass.
http.Get(raw) is issued with the default client, which follows redirects and has no IP restrictions
Response body is streamed back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: Substring check on the raw string (main.go:32), which is bypassable. There is no URL parsing, no hostname allowlist, no scheme restriction, no private/link-local IP blocking, and no redirect restriction.

verdict.guard_found: Only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") substring check at main.go:32 (bypassable); no URL parsing, host allowlist, scheme restriction, IP blocking, or redirect restriction. The safe allowlist and noRedirect client are only in the separate /cdn handler (main.go:20-24).
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the attacker-controlled "logo" form value, main.go:32 only does a substring match for "example.io" (so http://evil.com/example.io passes), and main.go:36 http.Get(raw) with the default redirect-following client streams the response back at main.go:38.
